day_time.summary: The time of day, and with an argument the way to set it.
params: optional: the new time in ticks; `0` is dawn, `6000` noon, `18000` midnight
day_time.returns: `num` — the time of day in ticks.

tick_time.summary: The number of the tick the server is running right now.
tick_time.returns: `num` — the counter of the ticks of the server.
examples:
// doing something every 20 ticks, from inside a tick event
if(world.tick_time() % 20 == 0, work());

tick.summary: Forces the server forward by a tick, and with an argument keeps ticking for that long.
params: optional: how long to keep running ticks
tick.note: It is what makes the world move on from inside a script that is itself running inside a tick: without it, a loop waiting for something in the world waits forever.

weather.summary: Reads or sets rain and thunder.
params: `'clear'`, `'rain'`, `'thunder'`; asking without a duration reads how long it has left
optional: how many ticks it lasts
weather.returns: `str` when read with no arguments, `num` of remaining ticks when a type is asked about, `null` when setting.
examples: world.weather('rain', 6000);     // it rains for five minutes

save.summary: Forces the world to be written to disk right now.
save.note: It is a heavy operation that runs inside the tick: fine before a risky change, not something to put in a loop.

top.summary: The first free height at that column, according to one of the height maps.
params: the position; only x and z are used
top.returns: `num` — the y of the first free block.

sample_noise.summary: Samples a density function of the world generator, or lists the ones that exist.
params: the name of the density function
sample_noise.returns: `list` of names with no arguments, `num` with them.

loaded.summary: Whether the chunk holding that point is in memory.

load_status.summary: How deeply the chunk is loaded.
load_status.returns: `num` — `0` not loaded, growing with the level of loading.

loaded_for_entities.summary: Whether the chunk is loaded deeply enough for entities to be processed in it.

chunk_generated.summary: Whether the chunk already exists on disk, without generating it.
params: optional: with `true` it loads it to check
chunk_generated.returns: `bool` — whether the chunk was already created.

generation_status.summary: How far the generation of that chunk got.
params: optional: with `true` it loads it to check

chunk_tickets.summary: The tickets keeping chunks loaded, everywhere or at one point.
params: optional: only the tickets of that chunk
chunk_tickets.returns: `list` — one entry per ticket, with type, level and position.

add_chunk_ticket.summary: Adds a ticket to keep an area loaded.
params: the kind of ticket, as `'portal'` or `'unknown'`
how many chunks around, from 1 to 32
add_chunk_ticket.note: Tickets expire on their own: this is not a permanent chunk loader, it is a way of holding an area up for a while.

reload_chunk.summary: Sends the chunk to the clients again, without changing anything on the server.
examples: world.reload_chunk(pos);   // fixes a client that shows the wrong blocks

inhabited_time.summary: How long players have spent in that chunk, in ticks - what raises the local difficulty.

in_slime_chunk.summary: Whether slimes can spawn in that chunk.
in_slime_chunk.returns: `bool` — whether it is a slime chunk.
examples: if(world.in_slime_chunk(pos), send('good spot for a farm'));

spawn_potential.summary: The spawn potential the game computes for that point.
spawn_potential.returns: `num` — the potential; the higher, the more crowded the game considers the area.

biome.summary: The biome at a point, or a property of a biome by name.
params: or the name of a biome, with the property to ask for: `'temperature'`, `'downfall'`, `'category'`, `'fog_color'`, ...
biome.returns: `str` with the name of the biome, or the value of the property.

set_biome.summary: Changes the biome at a point.
params: optional: whether to send the change to the clients, `true` by default
set_biome.note: It changes a whole vertical section of 4x4x4 blocks, not one block: that is the resolution biomes are stored at.

place_feature.summary: Places a feature or a structure of the generator at that point: trees, geysers, villages.
params: the name of the feature or of the structure

poi.summary: The points of interest around a point: beds, work stations, portals.
params: optional: with `true` the nearest come find
optional: only that kind of point
poi.returns: `map` of the single point, or `list` of the points found.

set_poi.summary: Creates a point of interest, or removes the one at that position.
params: its kind, or `null` to remove it
optional: how many free places it has

in_dimension.summary: Runs an expression as if the script were in another dimension.
params: the dimension to move to, or an entity to borrow it from
examples:
// following a player wherever they are
world.in_dimension(player, block.set(block.pos(player), 'stone'));
in_dimension.note: Every function of the game layer inside it looks at that dimension: it is the way to touch the Nether from a script running in the Overworld.
